text: Is this only an exam puzzle? Not really. The rule in Example 1 is a simple form of the Caesar cipher, one of the oldest known encryption techniques. Each letter is shifted by a fixed number of positions. The underlying idea, that information can be transformed by a rule and recovered by reversing it, runs through computing: Character encoding: your computer stores the letter A as the number 65 in ASCII. Encryption: secure communication uses far more complex transformation rules. Data compression: files are re-encoded into smaller representations. So when you practise coding-decoding, you're training the same pattern-detection skill that underlies how information is represented and protected. That's one reason this topic appears in C-CAT.
